title: Aegis Principal Identity v0
description: Canonical cross-PEP principal identity record: WHO an enforcement point resolved for a request, and HOW strongly that identity is bound. This is the identity analog of aegis-audit-event.v0 and the same shape used in that event's principal block. It models the LITE-to-FULL identity upgrade path explicitly via the assurance tier: static_key = an api-key→agent_id lookup (advisory self-identification, no cryptographic subject), core_issued = a Core-issued, signed, time-bound token whose auth_sub is the authoritative subject. Field names are snake_case. Secrets (the api key, the raw token) are NEVER part of this record (AO-005).

identity_schema_version.description: Canonical identity record schema version. Independent of each product's internal identity store version. Readers treat unknown higher versions as unverifiable, not as v0.

agent_id.description: Advisory self-identification (e.g. claude_code, kujouai). Always present. MUST NOT be treated as authoritative when a stronger binding exists; auth_sub supersedes it.

auth_sub.description: Authoritative cryptographically-bound subject. Present iff assurance=core_issued. This is the identity authorization decisions should bind to once available.

assurance.description: Binding strength. static_key = api-key→agent_id lookup (advisory only; no crypto subject; what AegisBase does today). core_issued = a Core-issued signed token (aegis-identity issuance) whose auth_sub is authoritative and whose lifetime is bounded by not_after.

issuer.description: Who issued the authoritative identity (e.g. aegis-core). Present iff assurance=core_issued.

not_after.description: RFC3339 UTC expiry of the authoritative identity. Present iff assurance=core_issued; static keys do not expire (an operational weakness this contract makes visible).

key_fingerprint.description: Optional NON-SECRET fingerprint of the resolving credential (e.g. a truncated hash of the api key id), for forensics. MUST NOT be the key itself or anything that could recover it (AO-005).

then.description: Static keys carry no authoritative subject, issuer, or expiry.
